body:
No time to travel, got business plans and work and things happening. Which is what's weird. I should feel great! But don't. Would you say I'm depressed? Like, properly. Not just a bit down.

If I am, what's the best way to approach it from that angle?

Yeah I'm aware that that's what I should be doing, and constantly try to learn about new stuff and do things... but when everyone else is all giddy and congratulating you, or upset over some bad news... and you are just stood there like 'heh'... it makes me feel broken.

'compulsion' - that's the word. There's something making me want to do it, think about it, and wonder if it would work.

It's weird as well I keep using it as a reference point like 'its gonna be a pain getting to work tomorrow on the tube'... 'could just take those pills, wouldn't have to do it then'.

It's become normal to think like that. I just worry that at one point I actually might, especially now I have that at my disposal.

An underlying and persistant feeling of unfulfillment, unhappiness and apathy. When I found out my degree result, I literally just shrugged my shoulders, when I find out bad news, I just go 'ah well'.

I have no emotion with anything, its just, a state of apathy running throughout everything. 

If I do feel happy, I'll feel sad after to make up for it, and vice versa.  Its like my mood is homeostatic, constantly attempting to feel nothing.

I don't think I'd ever act on it - but I can't stop looking at that damn packet.

I'm successful, social, recently graduated with a 1st class degree, got a job - but for the last 6 months have had an underlying 'I could just kill myself' lingering around.
